subject: Reserved pool - request for time-window throughput protection
messages:
From: Aisha Raman <aisha@clearsky.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved pool latency impacts — request for exception

Hi Olga,

Quick note from our ops team: over the past two weeks we've seen recurring queueing for our interactive endpoints during our nightly classification batch (01:30–03:45 UTC). The Dedicated pool we reserved is generally great, but when the nightly job runs it spikes token latency for human-facing calls up to 1.8s p50 and many tails beyond our tolerance.

We rely on low latency for our customer-facing flows and can't move the batch earlier due to downstream systems. Can Redwood provide either: 1) a time-window throughput protection (02:00–04:00 UTC) to preserve X tokens/sec for our pool, or 2) a carveout that gives our interactive traffic a higher queue priority during that window?

We understand this is an exception; we're open to a short-term amendment or a paid addendum. I've attached a short extract of logs showing the queueing spikes.

Thanks — really appreciate any path forward.

— Aisha
SRE, ClearSky Systems
attachments: clearsky-queue-sample-20270516.log

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Raman <aisha@clearsky.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved pool latency impacts — request for exception

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the detail and the log excerpt — that helps. We're sorry you're seeing that behavior. Short response: we can offer a couple of mitigations while we evaluate a formal SLA amendment.

Options we can stand up quickly:
- Temporary increase to your "burst headroom" for the next 30 days (adds ~20% available tokens during the window).
- Configure a time-sliced preemption rule so your batch gets scheduled on preemptible capacity outside the 02:00–04:00 UTC window.
- If you'd prefer a formal carveout, we can draft a Change Order for a time-window throughput protection (6-month term) that guarantees a minimum steady-state tokens/sec during 02:00–04:00 UTC, with rollback behavior and credits if we cross the threshold.

I've looped in Ben to outline pricing and Laura for legal/contract impact. To make the Change Order concrete we'll need:
- A sample SLA metric to guarantee (tokens/sec or p50/p95 thresholds)
- A clear runbook for fallback (what we do when the headroom is exhausted)
- Telemetry window so our product team can validate implementation feasibility (we saw your logs — more samples for different days would help).

If you're open, I can turn on the temporary burst increase right away and we can run a 48–72 hour test to validate.

— Olga
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved pool latency impacts — request for exception

Team —

Customer ask summarized: ClearSky wants a guaranteed throughput window (02:00–04:00 UTC) to prevent their batch jobs from impacting interactive latency. They're open to a paid amendment. Proposal: offer a 6-month time-sliced headroom addendum that guarantees a 20% headroom (measured as sustained tokens/sec guarantee with p95 latency target) during the requested window. If we fail to meet the guarantee, we credit X% of monthly fees (TBD).

Commercial considerations:
- We should price the headroom addendum as a monthly fixed fee on top of their reserved commitment; estimate: $8,000–$12,000/month depending on the exact tokens/sec guarantee.
- Need legal to draft a concise amendment and Product to confirm feasibility and rollout risk (esp. for multi-tenant scheduling).

I've attached a quick draft amendment for review (pricing placeholder). If Product signs off, I can share with ClearSky and start a DocuSign change order.

— Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-amendment-draft.pdf

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved pool latency impacts — request for exception

Thanks Ben — quick legal/product notes:

Product feasibility:
- Engineering: time-sliced headroom is feasible but considered a "beta" feature in scheduling; we'd want a limited pilot and explicit rollback controls. Implementation will require a configuration flag per Dedicated pool and a monitoring hook for automatic fallback to the customer's secondary model variant if thresholds are crossed. Ops/infra will need ~2 weeks to add the scheduling flag and test.

Contract/legal:
- We can do a short Change Order (6 months) that: defines the protected window (02:00–04:00 UTC), describes the metric (sustained tokens/sec with a p95 latency band), and includes a credit mechanism (percentage-of-monthly-fee) for breaches.
- We should add an explicit clause about maintenance and force majeure windows, and require ClearSky to share a monthly job calendar for scheduling coordination.

Next steps:
1) Product to confirm the exact tokens/sec baseline we can guarantee and the rollback runbook.
2) Ben to confirm pricing tier and present to customer.
3) Olga to offer the immediate temporary burst increase while Product builds the scheduling flag (48–72h test).

— Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: product-ops@redwood.ai, legal-approvals@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Aisha Raman <aisha@clearsky.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Reserved pool latency impacts — request for exception (ClearSky)

Forwarding customer thread and proposed amendment draft for expedited review. ClearSky is seeing repeated nightly queueing that affects interactive latency. Ben and Laura have sketched a commercial/legal path; product confirms ~2 weeks dev work to expose a time-sliced headroom flag and we can do a 6-month pilot.

Requesting:
- Product/Ops: confirm by EOD today whether we can scope the scheduling flag with a safe default (20% headroom) and a documented fallback runbook. If yes, provide a short Implementation Note we can attach to the Change Order.
- Legal: confirm the change order template and credit percentage range we should propose (suggest 5–15% of monthly fee on breach).

I'll enable a temporary +20% burst headroom for ClearSky now to buy time for the pilot; please keep me posted.

— Olga
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
